title: Epidemiology, treatment and outcomes of antimicrobial-resistant infections in hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients
authors: Estela Carvalho de Sousa et al.
one_line_summary: Recent findings support tailored treatment strategies and novel beta-lactams for multidrug-resistant bacterial infections in hematopoietic cell transplant recipients, alongside antimicrobial stewardship and optimized dosing.
key_pearls: **Ceftolozane-tazobactam** is the preferred agent for difficult-to-treat **Pseudomonas aeruginosa** (DTR-PA), demonstrating **superior** clinical cure rates and reduced nephrotoxicity compared to older regimens.

For **carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales** (CRE, mainly **KPC** producers), initiating **ceftazidime-avibactam** within **48 hours** **significantly** lowers 30-day **mortality** compared to delayed therapy (**16.7%** vs **50.0%**).
For **metallo-beta-lactamase (MBL)**-producing organisms, combined **ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam** or **cefiderocol** are the primary **recommended** treatment options.

High-dose **daptomycin** (**8–12 mg/kg/day**) is **recommended** for resistant Gram-positive BSI, as **daptomycin**-based regimens improve **survival** in **VRE** bacteremia compared to **tigecycline**.
Short-course antibiotic regimens (**7–11 days**) for Gram-negative BSI in neutropenic hematology patients demonstrate non-inferiority to prolonged therapy when stopped after neutrophil recovery.
population: Hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) recipients and patients with hematological malignancies (HM) presenting with multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial infections.

sections.heading: Epidemiology and Mortality Impact of AMR Infections in HCT
sections.content:
- Bloodstream infections (BSIs) occur in approximately **30%** of European patients with hematological malignancies or undergoing HCT, with **51%** caused by Gram-positive and **42%** by Gram-negative pathogens.
- Median extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (**ESBL**) / 3rd generation cephalosporin resistance (**3GCR**) reaches **30%** (range **6–51%**), while carbapenem resistance (**CR**) averages **13%** (up to **38%** in *Klebsiella pneumoniae*) and MDR *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* rates reach **29%** (range **4–37%**).
- Global pooled resistance prevalence demonstrates **21%** CR in Enterobacterales, **30%** CR in *P. aeruginosa*, **43%** methicillin-resistant *Staphylococcus aureus* (**MRSA**), and **41%** vancomycin-resistant *Enterococcus* (**VRE**).
- Antimicrobial resistance increases all-cause **mortality** (*hazard ratio* **1.72–8.96**); 28-day **mortality** for MDR Gram-negative BSI reaches **28.9%** vs **16.2%** for non-MDR Gram-negative BSI and **4.4%** for Gram-positive BSI.
- Inappropriate empirical antibiotic therapy **significantly** increases **mortality** in Gram-negative BSIs.
section_pearls: Inappropriate empirical therapy in Gram-negative BSI doubles the odds ratio of mortality in HCT recipients.
Carbapenem resistance rates among *Klebsiella pneumoniae* reach up to **38%** in European HCT centers.

sections.heading: Difficult-to-Treat Pseudomonas aeruginosa (DTR-PA)
sections.content:
- **Pseudomonas aeruginosa** BSIs carry **mortality** rates up to **38%**, with **33.8%** of neutropenic patients presenting in septic shock.
- **Ceftolozane-tazobactam** is the preferred agent for DTR-PA; the ZENITH study confirmed reduced 30-day **mortality** (**22.7%** vs **48.9%**, *p* = **0.005**) and lower mechanical ventilation requirements (**13.6%** vs **33.3%**, *p* = **0.021**) compared to standard therapy.
- The head-to-head CACTUS trial (**420** patients) showed higher clinical success with **ceftolozane-tazobactam** compared to **ceftazidime-avibactam** (*adjusted OR* **2.07**), though treatment-emergent resistance occurred in **22–23%** of cases.
- **Cefiderocol** therapy achieved **28-day** **survival** rates of **62.3–69.1%** in immunocompromised patients with MDR *P. aeruginosa*.
- ECIL-10 guidelines endorse combination therapy (a novel beta-lactam plus an **aminoglycoside**, **fluoroquinolone**, or **fosfomycin**) for DTR-PA in **critically** ill neutropenic patients or uncontrolled infection sources.
section_pearls: **Ceftolozane-tazobactam** yields superior clinical success over **ceftazidime-avibactam** for DTR-PA pneumonia.
Treatment-emergent resistance develops in **22–23%** of initially susceptible *P. aeruginosa* isolates during novel beta-lactam therapy.

sections.heading: Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales (CRE)
sections.content:
- **Ceftazidime-avibactam** is the frontline agent for **KPC** and **OXA-48** carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales.
- Early administration of **ceftazidime-avibactam** (<**48 hours**) reduced 30-day **mortality** to **16.7%** compared to **50.0%** when used as second-line therapy in hematology patients.
- The international TARZAN study in neutropenic CRE-BSI showed a 30-day overall **mortality** of **24.0%** and an infection-related **mortality** of **16.5%** when **70%** received adequate therapy within **24 hours**.
- For **MBL**-producing Enterobacterales, guidelines recommend **ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam** or **cefiderocol**.
- In the Phase 3 ASSEMBLE trial, **aztreonam-avibactam** demonstrated a lower 28-day **mortality** of **8%** (**1/12**) vs **33%** (**1/3**) for best available therapy in MBL infections.
section_pearls: Initiating **ceftazidime-avibactam** within **48 hours** reduces 30-day mortality from **50%** to **16.7%** in CRE infections.
**Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam** remains the preferred combination for metallo-beta-lactamase (MBL) producers.

sections.heading: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia Infections
sections.content:
- **Stenotrophomonas maltophilia** incidence ranges from **2.2–5.0%** in HCT recipients, carrying pre-engraftment **mortality** up to **60%** and median time to active treatment of **3 days**.
- Resistance rates to first-line agents reach **15.1%** for **levofloxacin** and **14.6%** for **trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole**.
- IDSA 2024 and ECIL-10 guidelines recommend combination therapy with **2 active agents** (e.g., **trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole** combined with **cefiderocol**, **minocycline**, **levofloxacin**, or **ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam**).
- **Cefiderocol** observational studies report clinical cure rates of **62–70%** and 28-day **mortality** of **30–37%** in *S. maltophilia* infections.
- **Eravacycline** demonstrated a **73.2%** clinical cure rate in a retrospective cohort, though neutropenic BSI representation was limited.
section_pearls: Due to high single-agent resistance, combination therapy with **2 active agents** is recommended for *S. maltophilia* in HCT recipients.
**Cefiderocol** achieves **62–70%** clinical cure in *Stenotrophomonas maltophilia* infections.

sections.heading: Resistant Gram-Positive Infections (VRE and MRSA)
sections.content:
- **VRE** BSI carries 100-day **mortality** rates of **83–100%**, serving as a marker of severe underlying illness and advanced disease.
- In a study of **517** VRE BSIs, **daptomycin**-based regimens (**8–10 mg/kg/day**) **significantly** improved 30-day **survival** compared to non-daptomycin regimens, whereas **tigecycline** was associated with increased **mortality**.
- High-dose **daptomycin** (**11–12 mg/kg/day**) improves target attainment for enterococcal and staphylococcal infections without increasing adverse events.
- Fifth-generation cephalosporins (**ceftobiprole**, **ceftaroline**) and long-acting lipoglycopeptides (**dalbavancin**, **oritavancin**) represent emerging options for **MRSA** management, particularly for outpatient conversion.
section_pearls: High-dose **daptomycin** (**8–12 mg/kg/day**) improves survival in VRE bacteremia compared to **tigecycline**-based regimens.
Acquired **daptomycin** resistance occurs predominantly in young, heavily treated HCT patients with repeated exposure.

sections.heading: Duration of Therapy and Antimicrobial Stewardship
sections.content:
- Short-course antibiotic therapy (**7–11 days**) for *P. aeruginosa* BSI in onco-hematology patients is non-**inferior** to prolonged therapy (**12–21 days**), provided treatment is stopped after neutrophil recovery.
- Seven-day targeted therapy for Enterobacterales BSI in high-risk neutropenic patients is feasible and effective.
- Antimicrobial stewardship strategies, including rapid de-escalation and limiting prophylactic fluoroquinolones, reduce carbapenem resistance rates (e.g., reduction from **22.0%** to **12.6%** over time).
section_pearls: Short-course therapy (**7–11 days**) for Gram-negative BSI in neutropenic patients requires documented neutrophil recovery prior to discontinuation.
Stewardship-driven reduction in prophylaxis decreases carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative selections.

strengths_limitations:
- Strengths: Comprehensive integration of post-2024 epidemiological and outcome data specifically focused on HCT and hematology cohorts; detailed breakdown of drug options by resistance mechanism (KPC, MBL, DTR-PA).
- Limitations: Reliance on real-world retrospective observational studies due to underrepresentation of immunocompromised recipients in prospective RCTs; heterogeneity in regional resistance rates limits universal extrapolation.

drugs_doses.dose: 1.5 g to 3 g IV q8h (dose-adjusted for renal function)
drugs_doses.indication: Difficult-to-treat Pseudomonas aeruginosa (DTR-PA) infections and BSIs
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Lower nephrotoxicity than polymyxins/aminoglycosides; risk of treatment-emergent resistance (22-23%).

drugs_doses.dose: 2.5 g IV q8h as 2-hour infusion (dose-adjusted for renal function)
drugs_doses.indication: KPC and OXA-48 carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales, DTR-PA
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Renal impairment, neurotoxicity at unadjusted doses, development of resistance during therapy.

drugs_doses.indication: MBL-producing Gram-negative bacilli, DTR-PA, Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, resistant Acinetobacter baumannii
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: All-cause mortality concerns in specific subsets, intrinsic resistance in S. maltophilia genogroup 4, elevated liver enzymes.

drugs_doses.dose: Combination or single co-formulation IV dosing (e.g., Ceftazidime-avibactam 2.5 g q8h + Aztreonam 2 g q8h)
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Transaminase elevations, diarrhea, rash, acute kidney injury in combination regimens.
Creatine phosphokinase (CPK) elevation, myopathy, eosinophilic pneumonia, emergence of daptomycin resistance.

drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, seizures (imipenem component), infusion-site reactions.

drugs_doses.indication: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia infections (part of combination therapy)
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Hyperkalemia, severe myelosuppression, acute kidney injury, severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCARs).
